No elected office held — and note a possible DISTRICT SWITCH: his Ballotpedia survey answer speaks of “representing all citizens in the 8TH congressional district,” suggesting an earlier candidacy or intent there. Verify before describing this as his only race. He entered politics in 2023, citing frustration over repeated break-ins at several businesses he owns in the state. Campaigns on law and order, affordability, and creating sustainable and affordable housing to address homelessness, along with lower taxes and parents’ rights. Lives in Normandy Park. TWO DETAILS HIS CAMPAIGN LEADS WITH: HE WAS ONCE A HOMELESS COLLEGE STUDENT, and he ASSISTED THE LIAISON FOR U.S. BORDER PATROL INTELLIGENCE. He owns SEVERAL small businesses, and says unity and collaboration are the keys to a better society — “fighting for each other and not against each other.” He is 40. Local coverage notes he balances anti-illegal-immigration positions with what he calls the essential role of immigrants in the U.S. workforce, and that he has posted AI-generated comics opposing birthright citizenship. The district takes in most of Seattle and Burien plus all of Vashon Island, Lake Forest Park, Shoreline and Normandy Park, with a MEDIAN HOUSEHOLD INCOME OF $119,340 — among the highest of any seat in this file.     Biography
    Republican nominee for Washington’s 9th District, advancing from the August 4, 2026 top-two primary with 16,842 votes (23.8%) behind Democratic Rep. Adam Smith on 50.9%. This is the SIXTH time the two have met: Basler was also the Republican nominee against Smith in 2014, 2016, 2018, 2020 and 2022, losing each time, most recently 71–29. He did not run in 2024. No elected office held; he was formerly senior vice chairman of the King County Republican Party and is currently vice president of the Eastside Republican Club. A pastor who owns a digital advertising agency. Campaigns on affordability and inflation, crime, homelessness and the global supply chain. Of the general election he has said he would welcome a debate: “I am happy to debate Adam Smith and listen patiently while he talks, and hopefully he listens patiently while I talk. Then we can either agree or come to the agreement that we disagree, but that doesn’t make Adam less than me.”

    Biography
    Republican nominee for Washington’s 10th District, advancing from the August 4, 2026 top-two primary behind Democratic Rep. Marilyn Strickland. He was the ONLY Republican among six candidates on the single open-primary ballot, which meant he collected the Republican vote by default; the field also included Democrats Adam Arafat and Alex Scheel and independents Kurtis Engle and Derek Maynes. The district covers most of Pierce County including Tacoma, plus Thurston County and Olympia, and is not competitive: Strickland beat Republican Don Hewett 58.7% to 41.3% in 2024 and Kamala Harris carried it with 57%. Strickland has held the seat since 2021, was the 38th Mayor of Tacoma from 2010 to 2018, and is the first member of Congress of both Korean and African American heritage and the first African American elected to Congress from Washington. PARTY STATUS — READ THIS BEFORE ANY CONVERSATION: on MARCH 9, 2026 KILEY FORMALLY LEFT THE REPUBLICAN PARTY AND BECAME AN INDEPENDENT, asking the Clerk of the House to reflect it on the official roster that day. He filed as a No Party Preference candidate and CONTINUES TO CAUCUS WITH HOUSE REPUBLICANS, so the majority was unaffected. He cited hyper-partisanship and the gerrymandering fight, saying “gerrymandering is a plague on democracy.” The House Republican Steering Committee REMOVED HIM from Education and the Workforce and from Transportation and Infrastructure after he left, THOUGH HE WAS LATER REINSTATED. He led the June top-two primary with about 24.3% to Democrat Richard Pan’s 23.2%, and the two meet in November. Pan is a pediatrician who served in the California Assembly and Senate from 2012 to 2022 and was once Kiley’s state Senate colleague. Kiley, first elected in 2022 with President Trump’s endorsement, is now campaigning chiefly against Governor Newsom and Sacramento rather than against Pan.
